notes: First run: open the site right after the install and create the admin account; the first visitor becomes the instance administrator. Further sign-ups can be turned off in Admin Settings.

Appsmith Community is one all-in-one container: the editor (Caddy), the Java backend, the realtime server and an embedded MongoDB and Redis all run under supervisord. Everything they keep, including the generated docker.env and the database, lives in the stacks volume at /appsmith-stacks.

APPSMITH_ENCRYPTION_PASSWORD and APPSMITH_ENCRYPTION_SALT encrypt saved datasource credentials. They are set from secrets so they do not depend on the docker.env the container writes on its first start (variables set from outside take precedence). Never change them: saved credentials cannot be decrypted afterwards.

APPSMITH_CUSTOM_DOMAIN is left unset on purpose: it makes the container's own Caddy request a Let's Encrypt certificate, while the panel already terminates HTTPS in front of it. Appsmith's Caddy trusts forwarded headers from private addresses by default, which covers the panel's proxy.

Memory floor 4g: the Java backend, MongoDB and the realtime server share the container. The first start is slow (several minutes) while the embedded database initialises, so the healthcheck (the image's own /opt/appsmith/healthcheck.sh) is given five minutes.
